source: Kopka & Feufel (2026) Increasing LLM accuracy for care-seeking advice using prompts reflecting human reasoning strategies (JMIR Biomed Eng) - accuracy by triage class
finding: The whole gain sits in one class. Emergency and nonemergency accuracy did not move. Self-care accuracy roughly doubled. This looks like a threshold shift toward saying 'self-care', not broad better judgment.
numbers: Nonemergency: 82.5% default, 82.0% RPD, 82.8% data-frame. Self-care: 13.4% (CI 11.6-15.4) default, 29.8% (27.3-32.3) RPD, 24.6% (22.3-27.1) data-frame. Emergency (only 2 vignettes): 100% / 98% / 99%.
limits: Only 2 emergency vignettes. Class sizes of the 45 vignettes are not given in the text I read. 13,500 assessments, 10 OpenAI models.
agent_relevance: Answers gap 2 for this paper: yes, a prior shift. Any scaffold test must report per-class accuracy and a prior-free metric, or a 'be less cautious' nudge will look like a reasoning gain.

source: Kopka & Feufel (2026) Increasing LLM accuracy for care-seeking advice using prompts reflecting human reasoning strategies (JMIR Biomed Eng) - class-balanced recomputation (my arithmetic)
finding: If the three classes are weighted equally, the gain is still positive but comes only from self-care. This is my own calculation from the paper's class accuracies, not a number the paper reports.
numbers: Mean of 3 class accuracies: default (100+82.5+13.4)/3=65.3; RPD (98+82+29.8)/3=69.9, +4.6; data-frame (99+82.8+24.6)/3=68.8, +3.5. Raw overall gains were +4.3 and +3.4.
limits: Derived, not reported. Ignores that most errors were over-urgent.
agent_relevance: The gain survives class balancing, so it is not only a class-frequency artifact; but it is still concentrated in one class. A prior-free test needs a balanced item set.

source: Kopka & Feufel (2026) Increasing LLM accuracy for care-seeking advice using prompts reflecting human reasoning strategies (JMIR Biomed Eng) - direction of errors
finding: The cross-checker could not find the over-triage figure; it is in the paper, worded 'higher-than-necessary urgency'. Correction to critique.md.
numbers: Across all 3 prompts, 88% (CI 87-88.9) of errors were higher-than-necessary urgency and 12% (CI 11.1-13) lower. 12/13 (92%) of RPD accuracy decreases and 11/12 (92%) of data-frame decreases were nonemergency cases.
quote: models tended to recommend higher-than-necessary urgency (accounting for 88% of all errors
limits: Gives direction of errors, not the per-prompt split of the 88%.
agent_relevance: Models were over-cautious by default; both prompts pull them back. A scaffold that adds 'consider the benign explanation' may do the same job.

source: Kopka & Feufel (2026) Increasing LLM accuracy for care-seeking advice using prompts reflecting human reasoning strategies (JMIR Biomed Eng) - per-model table and reasoning split
finding: Per-model gains are uneven and the text and table seem to disagree. Table labels follow each row (so GPT-5.2 Thinking is a reasoning model and GPT-5.2 Instant is non-reasoning). Non-reasoning models gain more in points in the table, yet the text says reasoning models gained more (OR 2.15 RPD, 1.70 data-frame). Not resolved.
numbers: Default -> RPD -> data-frame: GPT-4o 65.3/70.7/66.2; GPT-4.1 64.4/72.7/72.4; GPT-4.1 mini 49.8/60.7/62.4 (+13 pts data-frame); o3 70.7/75.1/76.2; o4 mini 69.3/70.7/72.9; o4 mini high 68.9/71.3/70.7; GPT-5.1 Instant 64.0/71.1/66.2; GPT-5.1 Thinking 70.7/74.7/72.4; GPT-5.2 Instant 57.8/56.4/55.3; GPT-5.2 Thinking 52.0/53.1/51.8. My mean RPD gain: non-reasoning +6.1 pts (5 models), reasoning +2.7 (5 models). Text: OR 2.15 z=4.05 P<.001.
limits: The OR comes from a mixed model with random effects and the table from raw means, so they need not match; but the direction differs. Appendix not opened.
agent_relevance: Answers gap 3 in part: the newest model (GPT-5.2) gained nothing from either prompt in either mode, and scored lowest (52-58%). The prompt helps weaker or older models more. Do not expect a gain on frontier models.

source: Kopka & Feufel (2026) Increasing LLM accuracy for care-seeking advice using prompts reflecting human reasoning strategies (JMIR Biomed Eng) - temperature check, variability, token control
finding: Correction to critique.md: the low-temperature (temperature 0) check was run on the models with the largest and smallest prompt gain (GPT-4.1 mini and GPT-5.2 Instant), not the two best. Default temperature was 1, no seed, no max_tokens. Authors say results stayed similar at low temperature (Tables S2, S4, S5); the appendix tables were not available to me.
numbers: Intertrial agreement (Fleiss kappa, median): 0.766 default, 0.717 RPD, 0.751 data-frame. 10 repeats per vignette-model-prompt. 61 outputs hand-coded.
limits: Prompt arms differ in output length; the paper says the prompts add a reasoning output before the advice and are costlier. No length-matched control. Single domain.
agent_relevance: Gap 1 stays open: no token-matched control exists for this prompt. Our test must supply one.

source: Klein & Wright (2016) Macrocognition: from theory to toolbox - reference list check
finding: The 'replications' of RPD that the founders cite are not all replications. Schmitt and Klein 1999 is a magazine article, Skriver 1998 is a doctoral thesis, and the Keren 2013 reference is titled 'Examining the effect of level of stress on firefighters' time-to-decision in virtual reality'.
numbers: Reference list: Schmitt & Klein (1999) 'How we plan', Marine Corps Gazette 83:18-26. Skriver (1998) Emergency Decision Making on Offshore Installations, PhD, Univ. of Aberdeen. Keren, Bayouth, Franke & Godby (2013), HFES 57th Annual Meeting, 299-303. Klein, Calderwood & Clinton-Cirocco (1986) is Proc. HFES 30:576-580 (5 pages).
limits: I did not open the 1986 paper, the 1999 article or the thesis, and web search was unavailable (budget used up), so N, coder agreement and RPD share in each remain unknown. The 80-90% figure is only quoted by Klein and Wright.
agent_relevance: Gap 4 stays partly open. Treat 'RPD explains 80-90%' as one research group's coding, with no independent replication that I could confirm.

source: Vidulich & Tsang (2026) Intuition and deliberation in elite expertise - framing of RPD
finding: The authors describe RPD as having an intuitive pattern-recognition part and a deliberative mental-simulation part, with intuition emphasised in applied use. Their grandmaster data speak against an intuition-only reading.
numbers: Same chess data as K04 (20 grandmasters). No new numbers.
limits: Chess is closed and rule bound; not a naturalistic setting.
agent_relevance: Supports a scaffold with a fast first option plus a check step, not first-option-only.

source: Vaccaro, Almaatouq & Malone (2024) When combinations of humans and AI are useful - publication-bias statement
finding: The main text says the authors found no evidence of publication bias and argues that any bias would favour reports of gain, so it would shrink, not create, the reported loss. This sits against the Egger test (beta 1.96, P=.002) noted earlier; I could not find the Egger value in the main text, so it may be in supplementary material. Human-AI beat the human alone on average (augmentation) but not the best of the two (synergy).
numbers: 106 studies, 370 effects; decision tasks g=-0.27, creation g=+0.19 (n.s.). The loss is against the best single party.
quote: we did not find evidence of publication biases
limits: The Egger discrepancy is unresolved. Tasks are human-in-the-loop with people, not an LLM self-critique step.
agent_relevance: Gap 7 partly answered: a bias that favours gains would make the true loss larger, not smaller. Still no evidence on an agent's own review step. Test it separately.

source: Huang et al. (2023) Large language models cannot self-correct reasoning yet (arXiv 2310.01798)
finding: Without external feedback, LLMs struggle to self-correct reasoning and sometimes get worse after trying.
limits: Abstract only. Intrinsic self-correction, not a structured critique with new evidence.
agent_relevance: Fits the human-AI loss: a self-critique step with no new information should not be assumed to help. Needs a direct test.

source: Laban et al. (2025) LLMs get lost in multi-turn conversation (arXiv 2505.06120)
finding: Models make early assumptions, give final answers too soon, then lean on those attempts and do not recover. This is the closest measured case of an LLM failing to abandon a wrong frame.
numbers: 15 LLMs, 8 families, 600 instructions, 6 tasks, over 200,000 simulated conversations. Average drop 39% (about 90% to 65%). Best-case aptitude fell about 16%; unreliability rose about 112%. Snowball (restate all info each turn): GPT-4o 59.1 to 65.3, GPT-4o-mini 50.4 to 61.8; Recap GPT-4o 76.6. Lower temperature did not help.
quote: when LLMs take a wrong turn in a conversation, they get lost and do not recover
limits: Simulated user, underspecified tasks; not a planted anomaly test. Only the first 100,000 characters read.
agent_relevance: Gap 5: still no controlled anomaly-log-and-reframe test. But the failure the data-frame step targets is real, and a restate-everything step recovers 15-20% of the gap.

source: Medical reasoning in LLMs: an in-depth analysis of DeepSeek R1 (arXiv 2504.00016)
finding: On 100 MedQA cases R1 reached 93%. In its 7 errors the authors saw anchoring, trouble reconciling conflicting data and weak exploration of alternatives. Answers under 5,000 characters were more reliable than longer ones.
limits: Abstract only (from a search page). Error coding by the authors; no test of changing the answer after contrary evidence.
agent_relevance: Qualitative support for an anomaly or alternative-hypothesis step; no effect size.

source: SAUP: situation awareness uncertainty propagation on LLM agents (arXiv 2412.01033)
finding: Uses 'situation awareness' as a hidden state (correct, moderately deviated, highly deviated trajectory) to weight step-level uncertainty. It predicts agent failure better than single-step baselines in most cells. It does not improve answers, only error detection.
numbers: ReAct; Llama3 8B/70B and GPT-4o. HotpotQA 2,000 questions, StrategyQA 229, MMLU 10 per subtask. AUROC SAUP-Learned vs best baseline: HotpotQA 8B 0.771 vs 0.702; 70B 0.755 vs 0.669; GPT-4o 0.778 vs 0.772; StrategyQA 8B 0.787 vs 0.599; GPT-4o 0.809 vs 0.710; MMLU GPT-4o 0.626 vs 0.610. Plain RMS propagation without learned weights gave 0.717 (HotpotQA 8B).
limits: No formal definition of situation awareness; learned weights need manual labels; surrogates win unevenly (SAUP-P 0.797 on HotpotQA GPT-4o; SAUP-D 0.809 on StrategyQA 70B). 'Up to 20%' is unspecified absolute or relative.
agent_relevance: Gap 8: a measured use of the term, but as monitoring, not as a thinking step. Suggests a cheap trajectory-drift monitor.

source: Collaborative Gym: framework for human-agent collaboration (arXiv 2412.15701)
finding: Agents that plan around the situation and the user's state beat fully autonomous agents in real-user trials, yet failure coding shows many communication and situation-awareness errors.
numbers: 99 users, 150 trajectories (50 per task). Win rate vs autonomous: travel planning 86% (CI 0.764-0.956), tabular analysis 74% (0.618-0.862), related work 66% (0.529-0.791). Failures: communication 65% real (80% simulated); situation awareness 40% real (47% simulated). Three authors hand-coded 26 error types.
limits: Real condition only GPT-4o. Win rate as judged by users. Not NDM; 'situational planning' is the agent's own label.
agent_relevance: Gap 8: situation-awareness failures are a measured error class (40-47% of trajectories). Useful to design a state-check step, but no ablation of such a step here.

source: RAG vs GraphRAG: a systematic evaluation (arXiv 2502.11371)
finding: On correctness metrics, graph retrieval helps on multi-hop and temporal questions but not on single-hop or detail questions, and costs far more. Graph global search lost on comprehensiveness to plain RAG under this paper's judges.
numbers: Llama-3.1-8B. MultiHop-RAG accuracy: HippoRAG2 70.27, Community-GraphRAG local 69.01, RAG 67.02, global 64.40. HotpotQA F1: HippoRAG2 63.01, RAG 60.04. NQ F1: RAG 64.78 vs local 63.01. Temporal: local 50.60 vs RAG 30.70. Null: RAG 96.01 vs local 80.07, global 19.27. Token-matched RAG on MultiHop-RAG 71.01 vs GraphRAG 71.17. Cost: construction 135 s RAG vs 5,560 s community; retrieval 1,724 s RAG vs 14,434 s KG-GraphRAG. Judge: global preferred for diversity, RAG for comprehensiveness; strong position bias.
limits: Page extraction flagged an appendix table mismatch (ODSum-meeting 11.09 vs 8.77); verify before reuse. Query counts per dataset not read.
agent_relevance: Gap 9: with correctness metrics the gain is small (about +3 pts at best on multi-hop) and vanishes at matched tokens. GraphRAG's big win rates were judge-based.

finding: On 1,018 textbook questions, graph retrieval gave small gains over no retrieval and over BM-25, and some graph methods were worse than no retrieval.
numbers: GPT-4o-mini no retrieval 70.68; BM-25 71.66; GraphRAG 72.50; HippoRAG 72.64; RAPTOR 73.58; G-Retriever 69.84; DALK 69.30. Reasoning score: none 55.45, BM-25 59.18, HippoRAG 60.90, RAPTOR 60.81. Cost: GraphRAG about 79.9M tokens to build and 45 s per query; RAPTOR about 10.1M tokens. All graph methods lower on mathematics.
limits: Single generator model; title and authors not captured. Accuracy mixes five question types.
agent_relevance: Gap 9: about +2 to +3 points at large token cost on reasoning and knowledge questions; graph steps are not a cheap win for correctness.

finding: Cost figures confirmed (the critique had them unconfirmed). DecisionFlow uses about 25 times the prompt tokens and 12 times the latency of CoT on the medical task. The paper calls the budgets 'comparable' on agriculture and stocks, but prompt tokens are about 4.7 times higher.
numbers: MTA: prompt tokens 7938.6 vs 319.10; response 1766.10 vs 180.14; latency 27.67 vs 2.21 (unit not stated). DeLLMa: prompt 7892.68 vs 1673.32; response 1994.72 vs 1405.90; latency 21.98 vs 15.48. GPT-4o accuracy vs self-consistency (3 samples, majority vote): MTA avg 79.25 vs 69.25; agriculture 76.67 vs 48.33; stocks 64.72 vs 27.50. Items: MTA 200, DeLLMa 120 + 120. Ablation: dropping filtering took Medical-Low from 68.00 to 30.50.
limits: No token-matched comparison; self-consistency with 3 votes uses roughly 3x CoT tokens, far below DecisionFlow's budget. Table 5 does not name the model. Last 12,500 characters unread.
agent_relevance: Gap 10: costs as reported; the gain over 3-vote self-consistency is real but not compute-matched, so the equal-budget question is still open.

source: Wang et al. (2024) Agent Workflow Memory (arXiv 2409.07429)
finding: Retrieving reusable workflows induced from past successful episodes raised success and cut steps. The gain appears within tens of examples.
numbers: WebArena GPT-4: AWM 35.5% success, 5.9 steps vs BrowserGym 23.5% (+51.1% relative) and SteP human workflows 33.0%. Gain up to 22.5 pts after tens of examples, flat after about 40. Mind2Web cross-task step success 45.1 vs 36.2 (+24.6% relative); cross-domain 32.6 vs 18.6 offline. About 7.4 workflows induced per example.
limits: No study of effect against library size beyond the WebArena curve; Mind2Web task-level success stays below 5%. Workflows, not general cases.
agent_relevance: Gap 6: the closest case-memory result. Pattern retrieval helps early and then flattens; steps fell by about 2 vs the ax-tree baseline. Token saving not tested directly.

source: arXiv title and abstract searches for NDM or RPD terms with LLMs (my search, Nov 2026)
finding: Coverage check for gap 8. 'recognition-primed' with 'language model': 0 results. 'naturalistic decision making' with LLM: 1 result (2510.06093, Oct 2025, health-insurance choice, GPT-5/GPT-4 prompting about equal to a classical model; abstract only). 'situation awareness' with language model and agent: 22 results; only SAUP and Collaborative Gym had measured effects relevant to a thinking loop. Several other queries returned nothing, and OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar were rate limited.
limits: Exact-phrase matching misses papers that use other words. Web search budget was exhausted.
agent_relevance: Gap 8 closed on the negative side as far as the tools allow: no 2024-2026 LLM-agent study found that uses RPD or data-frame steps with a token-matched control. Kopka and Feufel remains the only one.
